searches.reason: Develop paired sequence interventions—recent-history truncation, order shuffling, and removal of repeated recent themes—to measure whether rankings depend on current intent. Compare against matched random removals and popularity baselines, connecting sensitivity to sequence encoding and recency weighting. Use training-history prefixes and subsequent observed interactions without changing benchmark splits; report uncertainty separately for each dataset.

searches.reason: Build probes for the reported gap between broadly related recommendations and specific immediate relevance. Investigate hard negatives matched on popularity and title similarity, with distinctions such as artist, equipment prerequisites, or dimensions supported only by available titles and descriptions. Treat missing specifications and unobserved user intent as unknown; interaction absence alone cannot establish incompatibility, redundancy, or rejection. Connect ranking failures to negative sampling and scoring objectives.

searches.reason: Establish whether diagnostics identify actionable failures instead of reflecting score scale or sampling artifacts. Investigate controlled fault injection, bootstrap intervals, score-rescaling invariance, and agreement between sampled-candidate and full-catalog rankings. Test whether probe changes predict macro validation HR@10 improvements across the four datasets, with repeated-search uncertainty acknowledged. Replace unsupported zero results with explicit missing-evidence states.
